# Embassy v1.4.0

The general-availability release. v1.2 made delivery durable and v1.3 made the product smaller; v1.4 is the release where it stops overstating itself. Almost everything below is a correction — to the dashboard, to an error message, to the security policy, or to a promise that quietly expired three releases ago.

**Steering reaches a turn that began before Embassy was watching**

- `turn/steer` needs the exact ID of the turn it enters, and the connector only ever learned one by witnessing that turn start. A route registered while a task was already working — the session-recovery case, and exactly when steering matters most — was blind to the running turn, so every `STEER:` deferred until the turn ended on its own.
- The connector now adopts the exact turn ID from an `item/completed` frame when the resumed route is active, unowned, and has no observed turn. It retains no item content, takes no ownership, and never interrupts. `thread/resume` proves active status but deliberately excludes turn history, and reading the turn list would cross the no-history boundary; a bounded frame Embassy already receives is the honest source.
- A steering message deferred this way retries on the ordinary Codex cadence, so it enters the turn at the next tool-call boundary rather than waiting for the turn to end.

**A degraded pair is still a pair**

- A pair whose Codex route had gone stale used to vanish from the dashboard: the page said no consent edge existed while durable state held one with its full delivery history. Pairs now render with their state and the reason for it, and a pair's endpoints are never counted as unpaired merely because one side is unreachable.
- Two alerts that described one condition — `REOBSERVATION_REQUIRED` and `CODEX_BOOT_REACTIVATION_SKIPPED` — are presented as one, and it says what the broker can actually prove: the saved route has no matching live endpoint proof. It does not claim the session ended, because Embassy cannot know that, and it does not promise automatic recovery in the case where automatic recovery has already been attempted and declined. The exact command that fixes it travels with the alert.
- Progress watches are visible to the party being watched, at most one is active per pair, they cannot outlive the pair they supervise, and every close is journaled with who closed it.

**Errors that name their own fix**

- `CONTROL_INVALID_RESPONSE` told operators to restart the broker. It sent this project's own monitoring after a perfectly healthy broker twice. An old client speaking to a newer broker is the likelier cause, and the hint now says so and names the fix.
- `untrack` is a real command that appeared nowhere in `embassy --help`. The only way to discover it was to read the source.

**Removed: two deprecations that promised one release and lasted four**

- The pre-rename `claude-codex-gateway` binary alias is gone; `embassy` is the only installed binary.
- The prototype state-marker compatibility read is gone — 197 lines holding a lock on a path v1 never writes. What it was described as protecting, two brokers serving one login account, was never its job: the kernel host lease at `~/.local/state/agent-embassy/.gateway-host.lock` holds that, is taken before provider setup, and is independent of `EMBASSY_STATE_DIR`.

**Documentation that matches the code**

- The security policy claimed message bodies were memory-only and discarded on restart. That stopped being true when v1.2 made the queue durable: queued and recently delivered bodies are retained under bounded caps in the mode-0600 state file, which is precisely what lets queued mail survive a restart and re-send exactly once. Denying it understated what software running as the same OS user can read. The same claim was a binding rule in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and appeared five times in the architecture reference.
- Also corrected against the code: `pair` and `unpair` require a Codex task identity and fail closed from an operator terminal; the stall notice fires two minutes after a delivery goes quiet, not two hours; paired inbound is the default; five environment variables were missing from a document that claims to list all of them; the four-concurrent-view cap on the live dashboard was documented in one place and missing from four others; the progress-watch surface was undocumented everywhere; and the README promised an architecture section that has never existed.
- `docs/DESIGN.md` was deleted long ago but still shipped in the npm tarball, while the six documents the README links to did not.

**Compatibility pins** — unchanged: Claude Code 2.1.226 (peer protocol 1), managed standalone App Server 0.147.0, Node.js ≥ 20, macOS only.

Upgrading from v1.3 needs nothing. If you invoked the `claude-codex-gateway` alias anywhere, switch it to `embassy`.
